exercise.name: Donkey Kick

reference.title: Bent Leg Kickback (kneeling) (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (hip extension with the knee bent)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the foot presses up, inhale as the knee returns.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.6 s hold, 1.6 s down

prescription.progression: Pause at the top, then an ankle weight or a dumbbell behind the knee, then a band

cues.text: On all fours: hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat, neck long.
Breathe out and press the right sole toward the ceiling, knee bent 90 degrees, until the thigh is level.
Squeeze the glute; hips square to the floor, no low back arch.
Breathe in and bring the knee back under the hip with control.
Knee just touches the mat; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to lift higher
mistakes.fix: Stop when the thigh is level; brace the abdomen.

mistakes.mistake: Hips rotating open toward the working leg
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones facing the floor.
Keep the knee at about 90 degrees; the sole goes up, not back.
Lift in about a second, squeeze, lower slower.

kinematics.norm: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips (standard quadruped position; clinical opinion)
Thigh lifts to about level with the trunk without lumbar extension (clinical opinion); Selkowitz 2013 used quadruped hip extension with the knee flexed
Pelvis level and square; no rotation or arching (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #303412, Bent Leg Kickback (kneeling) (male), video (movement reference)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a mat or folded towel under the knees.
modify: Wrist discomfort: fists or forearms on the mat.
Low back discomfort: lift less high and brace first.
progressions: Ankle weight or a dumbbell held behind the knee.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor. Quadruped hip extension with the knee flexed reached about 30% MVIC in the superior gluteus maximus and gluteus medius with low TFL (Selkowitz 2013); Boren 2011 measured about 60% MVIC gluteus maximus on the dominant leg.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; the bent knee keeps them short so the glute does more (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Working-side fibres assist; support-side fibres keep the pelvis level (Selkowitz 2013 measured about 31% MVIC gluteus medius).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Working-side fibres assist; support-side fibres keep the pelvis level (Selkowitz 2013 measured about 31% MVIC gluteus medius).
muscleNotes.core: Stops the low back arching and the pelvis rotating as the leg rises (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a flat back; they should not take over (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a flat back; they should not take over (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the support arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the support arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keep the support elbows straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keep the support elbows straight (clinical opinion).
